title.narrative: WGG- Building Inclusive Movements and Alliances in Kenya

description.narrative: It is a strategic platform for activists to participate in and learn about differing viewpoints, form creative alliances and highlight issues that are generally considered to be beyond the purview of women’s rights and gender justice.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

title.narrative: Number of Young Women and Women with Disabilities collectives with increased capacities to conduct international human rights advocacy towards developing inclusive and progressive global norms on Sexual and Gender Based Violence(SGBV) and political participation

description.narrative: Due to capacity-building programs and support through the consortium, young women and women with disabilities and their organisations can conduct international human rights advocacy towards developing inclusive and progressive global norms on SGBV and political participation.

title.narrative: No of occasions young women and women with disabilities participating in various advocacy platforms at local, national, regional spaces

description.narrative: As a result of WGG's work, young women and women with disabilities are included in advocacy platforms: a place where they are often missed out\

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention,the baseline value is set at 0

(i) 4 podcasts hosted by Akili Dada in Kisumu and Mombasa counties focus on amplifying community issues on GBV and femicide - 2024 Feminist Institute Alumni were the guest speakers and content experts. (ii) KEFEADO through social media platforms and interactive media sessions: five sessions on TV Ramogi, two on Kala TV, and four on local interactive radio sessions to amplify women's voices. (iii) KEFEADO as panelists on youth issues including the support for the youth policy and access to information policy. This has ensured influence in the county engagements and policy frameworks in Kisumu. (iv) US Initiative: A radio talk show that engaged 400,000 listeners in creating awareness on the emerging trends of GBV and the role of the community in combating GBV. (v) KEFEADO facilitated one (1) young woman in Kisumu County policy review processes by creating linking and learning frameworks with the county.

A major outcome of the institutes was recording a podcast with the young women and women in media (this which can be accessed on Akili Dada’s Chini ya Mbuyu podcast under the titles “It’s about power, not how you dress”, Why not teach?”, and “Home is not a safe space anymore”.

A total of five podcasts were recorded. One was recorded with the young women and women in media (this which can be accessed on Akili Dada’s Chini ya Mbuyu podcast under the titles “It’s about power, not how you dress”, Why not teach?”, and “Home is not a safe space anymore”. Another four podcasts recorded where the young women also supported in organizing 16 days of activism campaign and some were session moderators. In addition to the five podcasts young women held two online sessions during international women's say in two different territories.Another engagement was as part of 16 days of activism.

Hosted three (3) virtual advocacy and capacity-building webinars, with participation of 75 women from the WGG cohorts, providing structured platforms to engage on key topics, including why movements matter, capitalist patriarchy, and distinguishing root systemic issues from symptoms. Three (3) county-level advocacy engagements in Homa Bay, Siaya, and Kisumu. The HANSAD reports capture young women's participation in discussions on women’s leadership and county governance structures. These reports provide verifiable evidence of young women’s engagement in local advocacy platforms, including their contributions, recommendations, and commitments within county-level policy and governance spaces.
